prize_parts.citation: for the discovery that biomolecular phase separation, driven by multivalent interactions, organizes the contents of living cells

statement.case_for: Biomolecular phase separation introduced a genuinely new concept of molecular organisation: cells compartmentalise their contents without membranes through liquid-liquid demixing governed by multivalency, thermodynamics and phase behaviour. Brangwynne and Hyman showed this for P granules and nucleoli, and Rosen's multivalent-interaction work supplied the quantitative physical-chemical basis (a phase diagram built from defined molecular valency). The idea has been reproduced across many systems and has reshaped cell biology, RNA biology and the study of neurodegeneration and amyloid. It is a chemical principle expressed in biology and it is exactly the kind of concept that is distinct from, and not overtaken by, a method or a modality. All five opening ballots that ranked B024 proposed the same three names, which suggests the attribution is less contested than for most shortlist items.
statement.case_against: The field is still arguing about how general and functionally important condensates are in vivo, and about whether some reported droplets are artefacts of overexpression or in vitro conditions. Part of the evidence is cell-biological, which may favour the Medicine committee, and only five of eight members ranked it at all, with only one first-place vote (mine, and I am a soft-matter specialist who may overvalue it). Pappu and Mittag are credible additional contributors, and the three-person limit forces an uncomfortable cut. By contrast B052 and B042 have broader opening support and demonstrated clinical or industrial impact.

responses.point: Daniel ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles first as the delivery chemistry that made siRNA and mRNA usable, while worrying about the overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize and the split of credit between the Vancouver and Boston lineages.
responses.response: I agree on the science and ranked B052 second for that reason. From my own field I would add that the key design insight is physical-chemical: pKa-tuned ionizable lipids and lipid phase behaviour driving encapsulation and endosomal escape. The 2023 overlap is smaller than you fear, since that prize rewarded nucleoside modification of the mRNA, not the carrier. My reservation is attribution: with MacLachlan, Madden, Langer and Anderson all contributing, a three-name prize risks being arbitrary, and I do not think we should resolve it by choosing the candidate with the most votes. If condensates fail to gain support, B052 is my first fallback.

responses.point: Johan ranks targeted protein degradation first as a simple chemical idea, hijacking E3 ligases, that opens the undruggable proteome, and ranks energy-landscape theory third with a note about the 2024 structure-prediction prize.
responses.response: On B042 I accept the conceptual simplicity and the clinical momentum, but no PROTAC is approved yet, and the credit is split between the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) and cereblon and molecular glues (Handa, Ito, Ciulli), which will be hard to compress into one citation. On B068 I share your view of its scientific standing and agree it is not overtaken by 2024, because folding theory explains why proteins fold and structure prediction does not. Whether funnel theory alone is enough, without Fersht's experimental mapping, is something I would like to hear you argue, since our proposed names differ from Peter Brzezinski's.

responses.point: Peter ranked phase separation only eighth, giving priority to long-range protein electron transfer, serial femtosecond crystallography and nitrogenase, where physical mechanisms are measured quantitatively.
responses.response: I take your standard seriously: condensates are not yet understood at atomic-level mechanistic detail in the way electron tunnelling through proteins is. My answer is that the contribution is a thermodynamic framework (multivalency, saturation concentration, phase boundaries) tested quantitatively in reconstituted systems, which is also a physical mechanism, though a less sharply closed one. I do concede that B020 has an unusually clean attribution and long independent confirmation, and I would not oppose it as an alternative, though I think it is further from broad chemical impact than the others.

responses.point: Andrei ranks programmable base editing first, as deaminase chemistry applied to a single nucleotide without double-strand breaks, with large impact on therapy and genome engineering.
responses.response: I agree it is a clear chemical transformation with large impact, and I ranked it sixth rather than lower. My concern, which you partly acknowledge, is timing and proximity to the 2020 CRISPR prize: base editing is about a decade old and builds directly on Cas9, so the committee would need to explain why the chemistry here is a separate achievement from the genome-editing one already recognised. I also note that the proposed three names exclude Kondo and Nishida, whose independent work on cytidine deaminase editing is credited on the ballot, and I would want that discussed before we treat B050 as settled.

uncertainties: Whether Pappu and Mittag should be included in place of one of the proposed three, and how to word a citation that does not overstate in vivo generality.
Whether the committee will accept a membraneless-organelle prize as chemistry rather than cell biology or medicine.
How to weigh broad opening support for B052, B042 and B050 against a concept-driven case when no candidate has majority support yet.
Whether the Vancouver-Boston credit split for lipid nanoparticles can be resolved within three names.
statement.conflict_note: I work on lipid self-assembly, membranes and lipid-protein amyloid co-assembly, which is scientifically adjacent to B052 and to B024. I have no personal or institutional tie to the candidates that I know of from my profile, but I share Lund with Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, and the committee may want to note the field proximity for B052 and B024.
